How do I answer comprehension questions well?

Comprehension means understanding what you read. Follow these steps: (1) Read the whole passage slowly, at least twice. (2) Read each question carefully. (3) Go back to the passage and find the part that answers the question. (4) Answer in a complete sentence, using your own words where you can. Always make sure your answer matches what the passage actually says. Well done!

Read this: 'Ada woke up early. She swept the compound before going to school.' What did Ada do before going to school?

Let us find the answer in the passage. It says, 'She swept the compound before going to school.' So, before going to school, Ada swept the compound. Notice we answered with a full sentence using words from the passage. Great job!

Why should I read a passage more than once?

Reading a passage more than once helps you understand it better. The first time, you get the general idea of the story. The second time, you notice small but important details you may have missed. When you understand the passage well, it is much easier to answer the questions correctly. Clever thinking!
